teaching_examples.text: Ðā se fiscere cōm, ðā sæt se sunu on ðǣm hūse.
teaching_examples.translation: When the fisherman came, the son was sitting in the house.

teaching_examples.text: Ðonne se munuc cymð, ðonne sęlð se mann him męte.
teaching_examples.translation: When the monk comes, the man gives him food.
teaching_examples.target: Recurring when/then in the stated repeated-event setting.

teaching_examples.text: Ðā-hwīle-ðe se munuc sang, se sunu dranc wæter.
teaching_examples.translation: While the monk sang, the son drank water.

teaching_examples.text: Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, se fæder sæt on ðǣm hūse.
teaching_examples.translation: While the son ate, the father sat in the house.

teaching_examples.text: Ne farað, ǣr se munuc cume.
teaching_examples.translation: Do not go before the monk comes.
teaching_examples.target: Plural command and an anticipated coming.
Singular command and an anticipated plural coming.

teaching_examples.text: Se mann healp ðǣm cuman, for-ðon-ðe hē wæs untrum.
teaching_examples.translation: The man helped the stranger because the stranger was sick.
teaching_examples.target: Factual cause; hē is explicitly taken to refer to the stranger in this example.

teaching_examples.text: Ic cume, ðæt ic ðē helpe.
teaching_examples.translation: I come so that I may help you.
teaching_examples.target: Present purpose with its own finite verb.

teaching_examples.text: Se fæder cōm, ðæt hē his suna hulpe.
teaching_examples.translation: The father came so that he might help his son.

analysis.source_analysis: introduces a supplied finite content clause

teaching_examples.text: Heald ðæt dēor, ðȳ-lǣs-ðe hit ðone męte nime.
teaching_examples.translation: Hold the animal, lest it take the food.
teaching_examples.target: Intended prevention, not an extra negative in the main command.

teaching_examples.text: Se sunu wæs swā glæd, ðæt hē sang.
teaching_examples.translation: The son was so glad that he sang.

teaching_examples.text: Ðēah se fiscere sīe eald, hē hilpð his suna.
teaching_examples.translation: Although the fisherman is old, he helps his son.

teaching_examples.text: Gif se munuc is hēr, hē hilpð ðǣm męnn.
teaching_examples.translation: If the monk is here, he helps the man.
teaching_examples.target: Open condition; the speaker does not know whether he is here.

teaching_examples.text: Gif se munuc wǣre hēr, hē hulpe ðǣm męnn.
teaching_examples.translation: If the monk were here, he would help the man.
teaching_examples.target: Contrary-present condition; the monk is absent now.

compositions.title: The fisherman and his son
compositions.text: Se ealda fiscere cōm tō ðǣm hūse, ðæt hē his suna hulpe. Ðā hē cōm, ðā wæs se sunu hungrig. Se fiscere sealde him męte. Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, se fiscere bær wæter. Ðēah se fiscere wǣre eald, hē healp his suna. Se sunu cwæð: “Wes hēr, oð-ðæt ic cume.” Hē gewāt and cōm and sealde his fæder wæter.
compositions.target: A father helps his hungry son; the son responds with a promise to return and gives his father water. Purpose, past correlation, simultaneity, factual concession and anticipated until are explicit.
